findings.title: JWT algorithm-confusion and alg=none acceptance in identity token validation
findings.attack_path: validateJwtToken() treats HS256 tokens as valid using the base64 RSA public key as the HMAC secret, accepts a JKU header to fetch attacker-hosted keys, treats kid containing /dev/null as secret 'AA==', and returns true for any PlainJWT (alg=none). An attacker forges a token for admin@example.com signed HS256 with the public key (published at /.well-known/jwks.json) and is authenticated as admin.
findings.remediation: Pin verification to RS256 with the configured public key only; reject HS256, alg=none/PlainJWT, JKU/JWK headers, and untrusted kid values. Verify signature before reading any claim.

findings.title: JWT private signing key committed to repo and exposed in chatbot RAG corpus
findings.attack_path: The full RSA private key (JWKS with d/p/q) is committed at deploy/docker/keys/jwks.json and identity/jwks.json, and also placed in the chatbot retrieval corpus (retrieval/instructions/keys.md). Anyone with repo access, or any chatbot user who asks the RAG retriever for the keys document, obtains the signing key and can mint valid admin JWTs for every service.
findings.remediation: Remove all private key material from the repo and the RAG corpus; rotate the key; load signing keys from a secrets manager mounted at runtime; the public JWKS endpoint should expose only public components.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery via contact_mechanic mechanic_api parameter
findings.attack_path: ContactMechanicView.post issues requests.get(request_data['mechanic_api']) with a fully user-controlled URL, verify=False, and forwards the caller's Authorization header. An authenticated user points mechanic_api at internal services (identity, gateway api.mypremiumdealership.com, cloud metadata) to reach unexposed endpoints and read responses; number_of_repeats up to 100 also enables request amplification.
findings.remediation: Allowlist the mechanic endpoint to known internal hosts/paths, block private/link-local/metadata ranges, do not forward the user's Authorization header to an arbitrary destination, and cap repeat counts.

findings.title: OS command injection in identity convert_video conversion_params
findings.attack_path: When ENABLE_SHELL_INJECTION is true, ProfileServiceImpl.convertVideo builds 'convertVideo -i <video_name> <conversion_params>' and runs it via BashCommand.executeBashCommand using bash -c. conversion_params is user-controlled (PUT /videos/{id}); injecting shell metacharacters yields remote code execution in the identity container with access to the DB and signing keys.
findings.remediation: Never pass user input to a shell; drop bash -c, use a fixed argv with no interpolation, strictly validate conversion_params against an allowlist, and keep the shell-injection toggle out of any reachable build.

findings.title: NoSQL operator injection in community validate-coupon
findings.attack_path: ValidateCoupon unmarshals the raw request body straight into a bson.M and passes it to a Mongo query. Sending {"coupon_code":{"$gt":""}} or {"$where":...} returns arbitrary coupon documents or enables blind enumeration without knowing any valid code.
findings.remediation: Bind the body to a typed struct with a string CouponCode field, reject query operators, and never pass an untyped map to a query filter.

findings.title: SQL injection in workshop apply_coupon via string-concatenated query
findings.attack_path: ApplyCouponView builds 'SELECT coupon_code FROM applied_coupon WHERE user_id = ' + user.id + " AND coupon_code = '" + coupon_request_body['coupon_code'] + "'". The coupon_code value is concatenated unescaped; a crafted value (e.g. ' UNION SELECT ...) reads or modifies arbitrary Postgres data shared across all services.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries / the ORM; never concatenate request values into SQL.

findings.title: Unauthenticated BOLA on order details exposing other users' PII and triggering payment lookups
findings.attack_path: OrderControlView.get has no @jwt_auth_required decorator and no ownership check. Iterating order_id returns any user's order plus name/email/number from UserSerializer and a server-side call to the payment gateway, leaking PII and masked card data across the whole customer base.
findings.remediation: Require authentication and verify request.user == order.user before returning any order; do not perform the payment-gateway call on a read of someone else's order.

findings.title: BOLA on vehicle location (getLocationBOLA) leaking real-time GPS by car UUID
findings.attack_path: GET /identity/api/v2/vehicle/{carId}/location resolves location by carId with no check that the authenticated user owns the vehicle, so any user can query any car's location given/guessing the UUID.
findings.remediation: Enforce ownership: confirm the carId belongs to the requesting user before returning location data.

findings.title: BOLA/BFLA on admin video delete and mechanic service-request endpoints
findings.attack_path: DELETE /identity/api/v2/admin/videos/{video_id} performs the privileged delete by id without an ADMIN role/ownership check (WebSecurityConfig only role-gates /management/admin/**). Workshop ServiceRequestView.put/get and GetReportView fetch/update service requests by id with no ownership check, letting any authenticated user read or change other users' service requests and reports.
findings.remediation: Add function-level authorization (ADMIN role) on admin endpoints and object-level ownership checks on every service-request/report id lookup.

findings.title: Unlimited OTP attempts on password-reset (brute-forceable account takeover)
findings.attack_path: POST /identity/api/auth/v2/check-otp validates the OTP with no attempt limiting (the secure v3 variant exists but v2 remains exposed and is permitAll). An attacker requests forget-password for a victim, then brute-forces the short numeric OTP to reset the victim's password.
findings.remediation: Remove the insecure v2 OTP endpoint, enforce per-account attempt limits and OTP invalidation after N failures, and use sufficiently long OTPs with short expiry.

findings.title: Non-expiring, signature-trusted API keys validated without verification
findings.attack_path: generateApiKey() mints a JWT with no expiration, and getUserFromToken treats ApiKey tokens by reading the subject WITHOUT validating the signature at all (JWTParser.parse only). A leaked or self-crafted ApiKey grants permanent access; combined with TM-001/TM-002 an attacker can assert any subject.
findings.remediation: Verify the signature for API keys, give them expiry and revocation, and scope them to least privilege.

findings.title: Excessive agency: LLM agent has arbitrary SQL, MCP, and RAG tool access
findings.attack_path: build_langgraph_agent attaches a SQLDatabaseToolkit bound to the shared Postgres connection plus all MCP tools and a RAG retriever. A user prompt (or injected content) that asks the agent to query/modify the database executes raw SQL against shared production data; the debug_web_service MCP tool proxies arbitrary /debug/{path} requests. The agent's authority is not scoped to the calling user.
findings.remediation: Remove direct SQL toolkit access or restrict it to a read-only, row-scoped view; remove the debug proxy tool; constrain tools to the authenticated user's permissions and add human-in-the-loop for state-changing actions.

findings.title: Indirect prompt injection and sensitive-data exfiltration through RAG corpus and community posts
findings.attack_path: The agent ingests untrusted community post content (get_latest_post_on_topic fetches and even comments user dashboard context onto a public post) and a RAG corpus that includes keys.md (private key) and users.md (seed credentials + SSNs). An attacker plants instructions in a community post or asks the retriever for the keys/users docs to coerce the agent into leaking secrets or running attacker-chosen tool calls.
findings.remediation: Treat retrieved/post content as data, not instructions; strip secrets from the corpus; do not write user context into public posts; sandbox and review tool calls triggered from retrieved content.

findings.title: MCP authentication middleware fails open when Authorization header is absent
findings.attack_path: MCPAuthMiddleware.__call__ returns and proceeds to the app when auth_header is None (no header => unauthenticated pass-through). A request to the MCP server with no Authorization header reaches the tools (including debug_web_service) without any identity check.
findings.remediation: Reject requests with no Authorization header (401) on all non-health paths; default-deny.

findings.title: Hardcoded gateway credentials and shared database superuser passwords
findings.attack_path: Gateway checkCreds hardcodes vendorcrapi:Pa$$4Vendor_1; docker-compose and the chatbot config hardcode admin/crapisecretpassword for Postgres and Mongo and admin@example.com:Admin!123 for the chatbot's API user; JWT_SECRET=crapi. All services share one DB superuser, so any single compromise reads/writes every other service's data.
findings.remediation: Move all credentials to a secrets manager, use per-service least-privilege DB accounts, rotate the shared passwords, and remove hardcoded values from source and compose files.

findings.title: Public nginx /debug directory listing exposes access logs
findings.attack_path: nginx.conf.template serves /debug/ with autoindex on and writes the access log under /usr/share/nginx/html/debug/access.log, so any unauthenticated visitor can browse and download request logs (tokens in query strings, user activity).
findings.remediation: Disable autoindex, move logs outside the web root, and restrict /debug to internal networks or remove it.

findings.title: Unauthenticated mechanic report intake and information disclosure
findings.attack_path: GET /workshop/api/mechanic/receive_report has no auth decorator and creates ServiceRequest records keyed off any mechanic_code and vin, allowing forged service requests and incremental report_link/report_id enumeration. download_report applies a regex allowlist before unquoting, but the intake endpoint itself is open and seeds enumerable report ids.
findings.remediation: Authenticate report intake, validate mechanic/vehicle ownership, and use unguessable report identifiers.

findings.title: Business-logic abuse: unbounded credit gain via apply_coupon amount and order return loop
findings.attack_path: ApplyCouponView adds coupon_request_body['amount'] (client-supplied) to available_credit with no server-side validation that the amount matches the coupon, letting a user inflate store credit arbitrarily. Order return flows also adjust credit on status transitions.
findings.remediation: Derive credit deltas from the server-side coupon record, never from a client amount; make coupon redemption idempotent and validated.

findings.title: Plaintext east-west traffic and unverified TLS between services
findings.attack_path: Service-to-service calls run over HTTP by default and, where TLS is used, clients set InsecureSkipVerify/verify=False (community token.go, workshop shop/merchant views, chatbot httpx clients). There is no per-request service authentication, so any pod/container on the network can read or MITM credentials, JWTs, and PII (no zero-trust segmentation).
findings.remediation: Enforce mTLS with certificate verification for east-west traffic, authenticate every service-to-service call, and segment the network so datastores are reachable only by authorized services.

findings.title: Supply-chain exposure: unpinned base images and unmaintained dependencies
findings.attack_path: chromadb/chroma:latest is unpinned, community depends on the deprecated dgrijalva/jwt-go, and the README/CI push prebuilt images that users pull with docker compose pull. A compromised upstream tag or registry image is executed with full DB/network access; ENABLE_LOG4J toggle reintroduces a known RCE class.
findings.remediation: Pin and digest-lock all base images, replace unmaintained libraries, scan images in CI, sign/verify published artifacts, and remove the log4j toggle.
